title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court and the People's Bank of China on Legally Regulating the Enforcement by People's Courts and the Assistance in Enforcement by Financial Institutions
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court and People's Bank of China
Notice on Regulating Court Enforcement and Assistance by Financial Institutions According to Law

Fa Fa [2000] No. 21

To: Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region; all branches of the People's Bank of China; the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China; the Agricultural Bank of China; the Bank of China; the China Construction Bank; and other financial institutions:

In order to protect the legitimate rights and interests of the parties and maintain economic order, in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the following notice is hereby given concerning matters related to regulating court enforcement and the assistance provided by banks (including their sub-branches, business offices, and savings offices) and other financial institutions that handle deposit business (hereinafter collectively referred to as "financial institutions"):

1. When a people's court inquires about the deposits of a judgment debtor in a financial institution, the enforcement personnel shall present their work ID cards and enforcement official cards, and produce a court notice of assistance in inquiring about deposits. The financial institution shall immediately assist in handling the inquiry, without requiring any signature formalities. The inquiry results shall be confirmed by the signature of the handling person. Where a financial institution refuses to assist in an inquiry despite complete assistance enforcement formalities, it shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 102 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Where a people's court needs to freeze the deposits of a judgment debtor that it has discovered in a financial institution, the enforcement personnel shall present their work ID cards and enforcement official cards, and produce a court freezing ruling and a notice of assistance in freezing deposits. The financial institution shall immediately assist in enforcement. Where a financial institution refuses to assist in a freeze despite complete assistance enforcement formalities, it shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 102 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Where a people's court is to deduct and transfer the deposits of a judgment debtor in a financial institution, the enforcement personnel shall present their work ID cards and enforcement official cards, and produce a court deduction and transfer ruling and a notice of assistance in deducting and transferring deposits, and shall also attach a copy of the effective legal instrument. The financial institution shall immediately assist in enforcement. Where a financial institution refuses to assist in deduction and transfer despite complete assistance enforcement formalities, it shall be dealt with in accordance with the provisions of Article 102 of the Civil Procedure Law.

When a people's court inquires about, freezes, or deducts and transfers the deposits of a judgment debtor in a financial institution, it may, based on the circumstances of the work, request the superior institution of the business premises where the depositor's account is opened to order that business premises to provide proper assistance in enforcement, but shall not request that superior institution itself provide assistance in enforcement.

2. Where a people's court requests a financial institution to assist in freezing or deducting and transferring the deposits of a judgment debtor, the freezing or deduction and transfer ruling and the notice of assistance in enforcement shall be subject to the provisions on service by leaving the document at the place of service.

3. Where a people's court freezes or deducts and transfers the deposits of a judgment debtor in a financial institution according to law, the financial institution shall handle the matter immediately. After receiving the notice of assistance in enforcement, it shall not deduct or transfer the funds that should be used for assistance in enforcement for purposes of collecting loans or interest; it shall not conceal or transfer the deposits of the judgment debtor. Violations of this provision shall be dealt with in accordance with the relevant provisions of Article 102 of the Civil Procedure Law.

4. Where a financial institution, after receiving a notice of assistance in enforcement from a people's court, leaks information to the party, causing the party to transfer deposits, the court shall have the authority to order the financial institution to recover the funds within a specified time limit. If the funds are not recovered after the time limit expires, the court shall impose a fine or detention in accordance with the provisions of Article 102 of the Civil Procedure Law; if the conduct constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be pursued according to law, and the relevant authorities shall be recommended to impose administrative sanctions.

5. With respect to the relevant materials that a people's court inquires about or inspects from a financial institution according to law, including information on the judgment debtor's account opening and deposit status, as well as accounting vouchers, ledgers, relevant bank statements, and other materials (including computer-stored data), the financial institution shall promptly and truthfully provide them and affix its seal; the people's court may, as needed, transcribe, copy, or photograph them, but shall maintain confidentiality according to law.

6. Where a financial institution is itself the judgment debtor, and the enforcing court inquires about its account opening and deposit status with the relevant People's Bank, the relevant People's Bank shall assist in the inquiry.

7. When a people's court inquires about the deposit status of a judgment debtor, if it provides only the unit account name but not the account number, the account-opening bank shall actively assist in the inquiry and provide a written response in accordance with the provisions of Article 2 of the "Notice on Implementing the Opinion of the Central Political and Legal Committee of the Communist Party of China on Issues Concerning the Freezing and Deduction of Bank Deposits by Judicial Organs" (Yin Fa [1997] No. 94).

8. Where a branch of a financial institution is the judgment debtor, the enforcing court shall issue to it a notice to perform within a time limit of fifteen days; if it fails to perform voluntarily within the time limit, enforcement shall be carried out compulsorily according to law; if the judgment debtor fails to provide property available for enforcement, the court shall, according to law, rule to successively replace its superior institution as the judgment debtor, up to its head office or parent company. Before each replacement, the replaced entity shall be given a time limit of fifteen days for voluntary performance; if it fails to perform voluntarily within the time limit, enforcement shall be carried out compulsorily according to law.

9. A people's court may, according to law, freeze the margins for bank acceptance drafts, but shall not deduct or transfer them. If the financial institution has already accepted the draft or has made payment to the outside party, upon the application of the financial institution, the people's court shall lift the freeze on the corresponding portion of the margins for the bank acceptance draft. When the margins for a bank acceptance draft have lost their margin function, the people's court may take measures to deduct and transfer them according to law.

10. In the course of enforcement where a people's court needs to execute two or more effective legal instruments rendered by two people's courts, or by a people's court and an arbitration or notarization institution, etc., on the same legal relationship, and requires assistance from a financial institution, the financial institution shall assist the court that first served the notice of assistance in enforcement by conducting inquiries and freezing, but shall not deduct or transfer funds. The relevant courts shall report the two or more effective legal instruments to their common higher-level court for coordination and resolution, and the financial institution shall act in accordance with the final coordination opinion of that common higher-level court.

11. Property preservation and advance enforcement shall be handled in accordance with the above provisions.

Where any previous provisions conflict with this notice, this notice shall prevail.

September 4, 2000
